card.name: Borborbor
card.tagline: Ewe social recreational dance of the mid-Volta Region
card.profile: Borborbor (also Akpese) is a Ghanaian and Togolese recreational dance performed by the Ewe of the mid-Volta Region of Ghana and southern Togo, including Kpalime and Lome (Wikipedia). Per Wikipedia, it is believed to have been originated by Mr. Francis Kudzo Nuatro in the 1950s, and is associated with Kpando, Ho, Hohoe and Peki. Mainly performed by women in colorful long garments twirling two white handkerchiefs, it features circular formations, waist turns and uplifting drum rhythms using vuga (master drum), asivu (support), vuvi, castanets and rattles (Wikipedia; Graphic Online).
card.insight: Cultural authorities describe Borborbor as a unifying, non-discriminatory dance now performed in churches and at state events - including as a curtain-raiser at Independence Day at Ho's Jubilee Park (Graphic Online).
